title: response-slab-attribution-notes
content:
Context / why: quick, exploratory doc for a new dashboard pattern ("slab attribution") to help SREs/product-engineers and platform users quickly find which portions of a generated response are driving cost and latency. We need something that scales better than per-token scrolling when responses are long (chat history, long generations).

Goals:
- Show coarse-to-fine breakdowns: slab (percentile) -> per-sample -> per-token waterfall on demand.
- Make cost attribution actionable: link slabs to model variants, quantization, batching policy.
- Enable fast triage: pin an invocation, replay tokens, export sample subset for evals.
- Fit into Console's current invocation inspector flow (left rail list -> center pane details).

Primary personas / jobs to be done:
- Platform engineer: spot tail-latency buckets and root cause (model, mem pressure, KV cache miss).
- Product engineer: understand which UI prompts cause inflated cost and clip/trim policy suggestions.
- SRE/Support: create a reproducible sample to file in support ticket.

User story examples:
1) As a platform engineer I want to view a single invocation and see which parts of the response contributed to 95th-percentile latency so I can decide whether to route to a cheaper model variant for that workload.
2) As a PM I want to identify repeated long tokens sequences (boilerplate) that cause extra tokens and cost so we can introduce truncation heuristics.

Design pattern overview (slab attribution):
- Slab concept: group tokens into contiguous ranges by runtime percentile buckets for that invocation (p50, p75, p90, p95, p99). Each slab is a horizontal band.
- Visualized metrics per slab: token count, token-cost (USD est), average per-token latency, total slab latency, cache-hit ratio (if available), model variant used.
- Drill-down: click a slab -> timeline of tokens (mini-waterfall) + sample replay controls + ability to highlight tokens that exceeded per-token latency threshold.
- Compare mode: select two slabs (or two invocations) side-by-side to compare cost/latency composition.

Wireframe notes (center panel):
- Top header: invocation id, model, region, timestamp, total tokens, total cost estimate, response latency. compact badges for: cached-prefix? kv-cache-hit-rate.
- Main area (left): vertical slab stack (each slab a row with proportional width showing token share) color-coded by latency severity (green -> yellow -> red). Hover reveals slab metrics tooltip.
- Main area (right): slab detail pane with token waterfall, small sparkline of per-token latency, and list of top contributing tokens by cost. Buttons: Replay, Export (csv/json), Create Eval (links to eval harness), Attach to ticket.
- Bottom: timeline scrubber with ability to toggle show/hide prompt vs. response vs. system tokens.

Component behaviors / micro-interactions:
- Hover slab: highlight corresponding range in timeline scrubber and in sample text.
- Click token in mini-waterfall: open modal with raw token text, embedding snippet, model logits snapshot (if permitted), and suggestion engine output (truncate, paraphrase, or compress).
- Replay: re-simulate token generation with same seed + model variant if available; visualize predicted vs actual latency. For privacy-sensitive orgs, replay is an anonymized dry-run.
- Compare: pinned slab(s) persist across selections until unpinned.

Data and backend signals needed (minimal viable):
- Per-token timestamps (or per-token duration) and token text/role.
- Model variant id and quantization profile used per invocation.
- KV-cache hit/miss per token range (available for recent runtime).
- Cost model: per-token compute cost estimates by model variant + bytes for embeddings/overhead.
- Aggregation service to compute percentile slabs for stored invocations.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Product: slab stack renders for any invocation > 64 tokens with p50/p90/p95 slabs computed.
- UX: clicking a slab shows token waterfall and token list for that slab in <200ms (client-render).
- Data: per-token durations available for 90% of sampled invocations in the last 7 days.
- Instrumentation: events emitted for slab open, token click, replay run (for metrics).

Metrics to track (to judge usefulness):
- % of invocations with slab view opened per team, time spent in slab view, number of exports/Evals created from slab.
- Reduction in support tickets of type "unexpected cost spike" where slab view was used.
- Feature adoption: fraction of power users (top 5 projects by spend) who pin a slab or use compare.

Prototype / visual experiments notes:
- Figma file linked in linked_artifacts. Early prototype uses stacked bars and a right-side waterfall. Consider alternative: radial slab (concentric rings) for single-invocation quick glance. Team feedback: stacked bars clearer for comparisons.
- Color palette must be re-usable in dark mode. Use mid-saturated oranges for p95/p99, soft blues for p50. Avoid green because cost-negative connotations.

Backlog + rough estimates (T-shirt):
- Backend: slab aggregator job and API (small) — 3d.
- Backend: ensure per-token durations retention for 30d (medium) — 5d.
- API: endpoint to fetch slab metadata + tokens page (small) — 2d.
- Frontend: slab stack component + tooltips (small) — 3d.
- Frontend: token waterfall + modal (medium) — 5d.
- Frontend: compare UI + pinned slabs (small) — 3d.
- QA/security review for replay (privacy gating) (small) — 2d.
- Docs + in-console tips (tiny) — 1d.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Slab boundaries: per-invocation percentiles vs. global percentiles. Per-invocation better for local triage; global easier for product-level KPIs. Possible solution: show both — default to per-invocation.
- Cost accuracy: do we show exact USD or estimate? Estimations are fine but need explicit confidence band. Add small "est" badge.
- Privacy: should replay be allowed by default? For enterprise/private deployments only if KMS/data-policy compliant. Add toggle in console settings.
- Sampling: storing per-token timestamps increases storage; do we sample 1:10 for long runs? Need SRE cost estimate.

Edge cases / gotchas:
- Very short responses: slab view should gracefully fall back to per-token waterfall only (no slabs).
- Responses with heavy function/tool calling: attribution should surface tool time separately (tool call latency slab).
- Combined invocations (multi-turn) — slab calc should allow grouping by turn. Add switch: slab by whole invocation vs. slab by turn.

Example flows (notes to devs):
- Flow A (triage slow tail): filter invocations by model + region + 95th latency > Xms -> open slab view -> identify slab where cache-miss high -> click replay -> create eval on smaller model variant.
- Flow B (cost-savings quick wins): filter by project + month -> open top 10 invocations by cost -> select slab that contributes >40% cost -> export tokens -> run automatic compression suggestions -> push change to prompt template.

Design decisions we made in meeting (2024-11-12):
- Use contiguous token ranges rather than non-contiguous high-latency token picks (tested by Marta; users found contiguous easier to reason about).
- Default slabbands to p50/p75/p90/p95/p99 (configurable).
- Add explicit "Create Eval" CTA early to close loop to Optimize product.

Next steps / immediate TODOs:
- [Ava] write backend spec for slab aggregator and estimate storage delta (due 2024-11-19).
- [Ravi] prototype slab-stack component in storybook (seed data) — sprint 12 spike.
- [Marta] run quick usability test with 3 internal engineers next week; focus on compare mode.
- [Samir] check replay privacy gating with security and list gating requirements.

Slip notes / scribbles:
- Consider small "auto-suggest" that recommends whether to route this invocation to a cheaper variant (rule-based: if slab p95 latency < threshold and cost delta > X).
- Maybe provide an aggregate "heatmap of slabs" for a query set rather than single-invocation to recommend model tuning.
- Explore combining with the token-inspector scrubber so both flows share state (avoid context duplication).

Meeting fragments / questions asked:
- Jordan: how important is per-token logits vs latency? Answer: logs/logits are helpful for research but gated by privacy; deprioritize in MVP.
- Product: want a single KPI tile to show "estimated monthly savings" if we auto-route top 5 expensive slabs to cheaper model. Place on project dashboard (follow-up doc).

Notes to self: keep this doc intentionally rough. Need to avoid overlapping with existing "token-slice" docs; this is focused on slab-percentiles and replay. Resist reusing "token-sleuth" phrasing.

If useful: quick mockup ideas (text):
- Column left: invocation list -> Column center: slab stack + scrubber + detail -> Column right: actions (replay/export/compare).
- Slab card: small bar, metrics row under (tokens | est $ | avg ms | cache%), gradient background. Clicking expands to show token waterfall with tiny bar for each token.

End of notes.
